content:
Yesterday we saw that Christ is the true bread from heaven, of which the manna was only a shadow. We saw that he is enough for the whole journey, and that Israel ate the manna for forty long years. We ended with a question.

One morning, after forty years of faithful provision, the manna simply did not come. Not one flake appeared upon the ground, and it was never seen again. Why did Yahweh stop feeding His people in this way? Today we find the answer, and it is full of hope.

First, notice that the manna did not stop halfway through the desert.

Yahweh did not feed Israel for thirty-nine years and then leave them hungry at the border. He continued His provision until they actually reached the land. Exodus 16:35 says, "They ate manna until they came to the border of the land of Canaan." This is full of comfort for us. The bread lasted exactly as long as the journey lasted. Yahweh's provision did not fail before the journey was complete. And in the same way, Yahweh will not begin a good work in us and then abandon us before the end. Paul says, "And I am certain that God, who began the good work within you, will continue his work until it is finally finished" (Philippians 1:6). The same Father who called us will feed us.The same Father who began the journey will carry us through it. The same Father who gave the bread today will provide what is needed tomorrow.His faithful provision will continue right up to the day when we meet Christ.

Then came the day when the manna stopped. When Israel crossed the Jordan and entered Canaan, they began to eat the produce of the Promised Land. Joshua 5:11-12 says, "The very next day they began to eat unleavened bread and roasted grain harvested from the land. No manna appeared on the day they first ate from the crops of the land, and it was never seen again." So the manna did not stop because Yahweh had forgotten them. It stopped because something better had finally arrived. This is a beautiful picture. Manna was food for pilgrims. The produce of Canaan was food for possessors.

Manna belonged to the wilderness journey. The fruit of the land belonged to the inheritance.

In the same way, we now gather truth day by day. We know in part. We learn in parts. We gather flake by flake, verse by verse, lesson by lesson. But the day is coming when the wilderness journey will be over. John says, "We will be like him, for we will see him as he really is" (1 John 3:2). Paul says, "Now I know in part; then I will know everything completely" (1 Corinthians 13:12). Now we study the truth from below. Then we shall stand in the glory of what Yahweh has promised. Now we walk by faith. Then faith will give way to sight.

Now we gather the manna of the wilderness. Then we shall eat the fruit of the inheritance, the divine nature.

Peter tells us that Yahweh has given us precious promises, "These are the promises that enable you to share his divine nature" (2 Peter 1:4). And Paul says of the resurrection body, "It is sown in weakness, but it is raised in strength.

It is sown a natural human body, but it is raised a spiritual body" (1 Corinthians 15:43-44). He also says, "Our dying bodies must be transformed into bodies that will never die; our mortal bodies must be transformed into immortal bodies"(1 Corinthians 15:53). So when the faithful are changed into the image of Christ and raised in immortality, the daily gathering of wilderness manna will no longer be needed. The pilgrim's bread will give way to the fruit of the land.

And here is another wonder. Once the manna stopped, it never appeared again. Not a single flake fell upon the fields of Canaan. There was no need to go back to wilderness food, because the wilderness journey was finished. In the same way, once the faithful enter their inheritance, the days of hunger, searching, weakness, and daily struggle will never return. The trial is only for a time, but the glory is eternal. Paul says, "For our present troubles are small and won't last very long. Yet they produce for us a glory that vastly outweighs them and will last forever!" (2 Corinthians 4:17). The wilderness does not last forever.

The gathering does not last forever. The hunger does not last forever. The daily struggle does not last forever. Yahweh has placed an end before His people, and that end is glory.

Yet Yahweh also commanded that a golden jar of manna be preserved before Him as a memorial. Exodus 16:33 says, "Get a jar and fill it with two quarts of manna. Then put it in a sacred place before the LORD to preserve it for all future generations." And our Master gives this precious promise, "To everyone who is victorious I will give some of the manna that has been hidden away in heaven" (Revelation 2:17). So the wilderness bread will not be forgotten. It will remain as a lasting testimony of Yahweh's faithfulness. The hidden manna reminds us that Yahweh fed His people every single day until the journey was complete. He did not forget them in the desert. He did not leave them hungry.
He provided faithfully until the promise was reached.

Therefore, let us feed daily on the true bread from heaven. Let us receive the words of Christ. Let us follow his example. Let us trust that what Yahweh has provided is enough for the whole journey. Let us not turn back to Egypt or go searching for another food for our souls. The manna sustained Israel until Canaan. Christ will sustain us until the inheritance. The bread from heaven will not fail before the journey is done. And so, we come to the end of our study of the manna. Yahweh willing, we will step into a new lesson tomorrow.

title: Prayer
text:
Our loving Father Yahweh,

We thank You that Your provision lasted as long as the journey lasted,

and that You will finish the good work You have begun in us.

Feed us daily on the true bread from heaven, Your beloved Son.

Keep us faithful until the day we cross over into our inheritance,

when faith will give way to sight and the gathering will be over forever.

May we be counted among the overcomers who receive the hidden manna.

"Spend your energy seeking the eternal life that the Son of Man can give you." - John 6:27

In the name of Christ our Messiah, we pray. Amen.
